title: close_thread releases the pointer only when it names the thread being closed, and only after the commit
context: close_thread moved a thread to a terminal state without releasing the active-thread pointer, so a session that closed and stopped left a pointer naming a terminal thread, and a park_thread on a different open thread was refused for naming the closed one. Three shapes were on the table: release inside close_thread, make the pointer read treat a terminal thread as absent, or both. The release also had to answer what happens when the pointer names a different thread than the one being closed, where an unconditional release would take another session's hold.
options: close_thread calls releasePointerIfOwned with the closed thread id, after the ledger commit succeeds
the pointer read treats a pointer naming a terminal thread as absent, leaving the file on disk
both, releasing in close_thread and hiding terminal-named pointers on read
outcome: close_thread calls releasePointerIfOwned with the id of the thread it just closed, immediately after the ledger commit succeeds, and reports nothing new in its output. The release is conditional on the pointer naming that same thread, so a pointer naming a different thread is left untouched and no other session's hold is taken. A pointer naming the closed thread is released even when a different session wrote it, because a terminal thread can no longer be resumed, parked with an outcome or updated, so that hold protects nothing, and park_thread already releases a terminal-named pointer by the same thread-id-only rule. Making the pointer read treat a terminal thread as absent was rejected because it would hide the file rather than delete it, would stop releasePointerIfOwned from ever unlinking it, and would make park_thread's terminal-pointer-released branch unreachable. The release goes after the commit so that a refused close never gives up a hold the session still needs in order to park with an outcome.
